added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(K=4\), let \(\mathcal X=\{x\}\), and let \(\rho(x)=1\).  For every \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) and \(m_*\in(0,1)\), put \(M_0=(1+m_*)/2\).  There are an explicitly constructed \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), a direction \(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\), and \(r_0>0\) such that \(M(p)=M_0\) and, for every \(0<r\le r_0\),
\[
 E_{p,r}(g)=0,
 \qquad
 E_{p,r}(-g)\ge M_0^{-1}.
\]
Consequently the ray-restricted oriented functional \(W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(tg)=(-t)_+/M_0\) satisfies \(W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(tg)\le E_{p,r}(tg)\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\), while \(W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(g)=0\) and \(W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(-g)=M_0^{-1}>0\).  Moreover, for every sufficiently small \(\tau\in(0,r)\), the ambient law \(q_\tau=p-\tau g\) and an explicit legal base \(b_\tau\in\mathcal B(p,r)\) obey
\[
 \left\|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q_\tau)-\Phi(p)\right\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau}{M_0-2\tau}
 \le \left\|d_{b_\tau}(-\tau g)\right\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau M_0}{(M_0-2\tau)^2}.
\]
Thus retaining orientation repairs both the parity contradiction and the finite-curvature comparison on the accepted singleton-cell witness; this lemma makes no claim about simultaneous faces outside that witness.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Define
\[
 \ell=M_0\left(\frac18,\frac18,\frac3{10},\frac9{20}\right),
 \qquad
 h=M_0\left(\frac14,\frac14,\frac14,\frac14\right),
 \qquad
 \gamma_{ij}=\frac{\ell_i h_j}{M_0}.
\tag{1}
\]
Give latent complier-survivor type
\[
 C_{ij}=(d_0,d_1,s_0,s_1,y_0,y_1)=(0,1,1,1,i,j)
\]
mass \(\gamma_{ij}\), give the never-taker never-selected type
\(N=(0,0,0,0,0,0)\) mass \((1-M_0)/2\), and give the always-taker never-selected type \(A=(1,1,0,0,0,0)\) mass \((1-M_0)/2\).  Since
\[
 \sum_{i,j=0}^3\gamma_{ij}
 =M_0^{-1}\left(\sum_i\ell_i\right)\left(\sum_jh_j\right)=M_0,
\tag{2}
\]
these nonnegative masses sum to one.  Draw \(Z\) independently of the latent type with probability one half, and apply the three consistency relations.  Independence proves \(\text{ass:conditional-iv-independence}\); the construction proves \(\text{ass:consistency}\), \(\text{ass:selection-consistency}\), and \(\text{ass:outcome-consistency}\).  Every type has \(d_0\le d_1\), and every complier has \(s_1-s_0=0\), proving \(\text{ass:no-defiers}\) and \(\text{ass:cellwise-selection-monotonicity}\).  Finally, \(1/2\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), so \(\text{ass:instrument-overlap}\) holds.

Let \(p\) be the induced observed law.  Substitution in \(\text{def:capacity-map}\) gives
\[
 q_{x0}(p)=q_{x1}(p)=\frac12,
 \qquad H_x(p)=(\ell,h),
 \qquad M(p)=M_0\ge m_*.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) by \(\text{def:legal-model}\) and \(\text{def:observed-law-image}\).  The lower-minus-upper prefix differences and the upper-cut values are, respectively,
\[
 M_0\left(-\frac18,-\frac14,-\frac15,0\right)
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 M_0\left(\frac34,\frac58,\frac12,\frac{11}{20}\right).
\tag{4}
\]
Therefore the lower numerator is zero, the unique upper cut is \(t=2\), its numerator is \(M_0/2\), and
\[
 \Phi(p)=\left(0,\frac12\right).
\tag{5}
\]

Let
\[
 u=(x,1,(1,1,1)),\qquad v=(x,1,(0,0,0)),
 \qquad g=e_u-e_v.
\tag{6}
\]
This direction preserves both instrument-arm masses.  At any sufficiently nearby legal base \(b\), all capacity coordinates remain positive, the proper prefix inequalities and the unique upper cut in \((4)\) persist, and increasing selection monotonicity gives \(s_1(b)\ge s_0(b)\).  Direct differentiation of the conditional contrasts therefore gives
\[
 D H_x(b)[g]=(0,0,0,0;0,q_{x1}(b)^{-1},0,0).
\tag{7}
\]
The direction in \((7)\) leaves the lower numerator, the unique upper numerator, and \(\min\{s_0(b),s_1(b)\}=s_0(b)\) unchanged.  The quotient rule in \(\text{def:endpoint-map}\) hence yields \(d_b(g)=0\).  Compactness of the strict inequalities in \((4)\) supplies \(r_0>0\) for which this conclusion holds for every \(b\in\mathcal B(p,r)\) and every \(0<r\le r_0\).  By \(\text{def:deterministic-inner-envelope}\),
\[
 E_{p,r}(g)=0.
\tag{8}
\]

At the tied base \(p\), direction \(-g\) lowers the upper total at rate two and leaves the active upper numerator fixed.  Hence
\[
 \partial_+M(p;-g)=-2,
 \qquad
 \partial_+\bar N_U(p;-g)=0,
 \qquad
 d_{p,U}(-g)=\frac{1}{M_0}.
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(p\in\mathcal B(p,r)\), equations \((8)\)--\((9)\) and positive homogeneity in a nonnegative scalar imply
\[
 E_{p,r}(-g)\ge M_0^{-1},
 \qquad
 W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(tg)=\frac{(-t)_+}{M_0}le E_{p,r}(tg)
 \quad(t\in\mathbb R).
\tag{10}
\]
This proves the oriented parity assertion.

It remains to verify the finite increment rather than only its tangent.  Both \(u\) and \(v\) have positive \(p\)-mass.  For sufficiently small \(\tau>0\), \(q_\tau=p-\tau g\) is therefore a probability vector with support contained in that of \(p\).  Its capacity pair and endpoint are
\[
 H_x(q_\tau)=(\ell,h-2\tau e_1),
 \qquad M(q_\tau)=M_0-2\tau,
 \qquad
 \Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q_\tau)
 =\left(0,\frac{M_0/2}{M_0-2\tau}\right).
\tag{11}
\]
The cut calculation in \((4)\) remains strict when \(\tau\) is small, so \((11)\) follows directly from \(\text{def:capacity-map}\) and \(\text{def:endpoint-map}\).  It gives
\[
 \left\|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q_\tau)-\Phi(p)\right\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau}{M_0-2\tau}.
\tag{12}
\]

Now introduce the initially zero complier never-selected type
\[
 R=(0,1,0,0,0,0).
\]
Construct a full law for \(b_\tau\) by transferring latent mass \(2\tau\) from \(C_{31}\) to \(R\), leaving every other latent mass and the instrument propensity fixed.  This is feasible whenever
\[
 2\tau\le\gamma_{31}=\frac{9M_0}{80}.
\tag{13}
\]
Both donor and recipient are compliers, both obey \(s_1-s_0=0\), and the propensity is unchanged.  Thus every declared structural restriction remains true.  The transfer reduces both survivor margins by \(2\tau\), so
\[
 H_x(b_\tau)=(\ell-2\tau e_3,h-2\tau e_1),
 \qquad M(b_\tau)=M_0-2\tau.
\tag{14}
\]
Choose \(\tau<(M_0-m_*)/2\); then the aggregate-mass restriction also remains true.  Under each instrument value the conditional observed mass transfer is \(2\tau\), while the propensity is one half, and therefore
\[
 \|b_\tau-p\|_\infty=\tau<r.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus \(b_\tau\in\mathcal B(p,r)\).  Neither removed coordinate occurs in the active upper cut \(t=2\), so \(\bar N_U(b_\tau)=M_0/2\).  The same prefix calculation as in \((4)\) shows that the lower numerator is locally zero both before and after an infinitesimal displacement in direction \(-g\).  The two totals in \((14)\) are tied.  Applying direction \(-g\) at this base leaves the active upper numerator fixed and lowers the upper total at rate two.  The quotient rule gives
\[
 d_{b_\tau,U}(-g)
 =\frac{2(M_0/2)}{(M_0-2\tau)^2}
 =\frac{M_0}{(M_0-2\tau)^2}.
\tag{16}
\]
Positive homogeneity, \((12)\), and \((16)\) yield
\[
 \left\|d_{b_\tau}(-\tau g)\right\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau M_0}{(M_0-2\tau)^2}
 \ge\frac{\tau}{M_0-2\tau}
 =\left\|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q_\tau)-\Phi(p)\right\|_\infty.
\]
This is the claimed explicit nearby-legal-base domination.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct and prove the global finite face-indexed non-even comparison required by the directive: an oriented functional \(W_{p,r}\) with pointwise \(W_{p,r}(z)\le E_{p,r}(z)\), signed finite-increment domination for every nearby empirical law, row-by-row covariance traction, and conditional lower-quantile transfer, including the exact-zero-scale branch.
open_obligations.obstruction: At a selection-total boundary the required orientation is available, but at intersections with raw-capacity zeros and tied lower or upper cuts the endpoint derivative is a quotient of nested one-sided minima and maxima.  Extracting a candidate positive-part face row does not itself prove that the row is pointwise bounded by the norm of the full directional derivative: numerator, denominator, and tied-cut terms can cancel for directions outside the row's originating cone.  Legalizing a face by a latent donor transfer also changes both donor outcome margins, so coefficient inclusion and the claimed bound \(s_{p,r}\ge c r A_{p,r}\) must be checked for the complete transfer matrix.  Those checks, and therefore the relative non-even Gaussian quantile theorem, are absent from the frozen primitives and were not closed here.
open_obligations.attempted: I separated smooth interior faces from the one-sided selection-total face, retained signed positive parts instead of absolute linear rows, and tested the accepted singleton-cell counterexample.  The explicit transfer from survivor type \(C_{31}\) to a never-selected complier proves that orientation fixes both parity and finite ratio curvature on that witness.  I then tried to extend the construction by assigning smooth probes to untied cut faces and boundary probes to selection-total faces.  The extension stops at simultaneous faces because a local face coefficient can be canceled by another active quotient term outside its direction cone; no pointwise oriented property \((\mathrm{P1})\) or row-by-row traction certificate follows merely from finite face enumeration.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The oriented repair passes the directive's accepted singleton-cell test.  In the explicit \(K=4\) law of \(\text{lem:k4-oriented-parity-certificate}\), the legally inward direction satisfies \(E_{p,r}(g)=0\), whereas \(E_{p,r}(-g)\ge M_0^{-1}\); hence \(W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(tg)=(-t)_+/M_0\) has exactly the required parity.  More strongly, moving mass \(2\tau\) from survivor type \(C_{31}\) to a never-selected complier produces a legal base \(b_\tau\) with \(\|b_\tau-p\|_\infty=\tau\), and
\[
 \|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(p-\tau g)-\Phi(p)\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau}{M_0-2\tau}
 \le\|d_{b_\tau}(-\tau g)\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau M_0}{(M_0-2\tau)^2}.
\]
Thus the previous contradiction was caused by even symmetrization and is repaired on that face.  Uniform concentration still gives \(\|\widehat p_n-p_n\|_\infty=o_{P_n}(a_n)\), so the deterministic inner ball is contained in \(B_n\) with probability tending to one uniformly.  What has not been proved is the global oriented analogue of the former properties \((\mathrm{P1})\)--\((\mathrm{P3})\): a finite row set whose positive parts are pointwise bounded by \(E_{p,r}\) for every direction, which dominates every signed endpoint increment after all simultaneous sign, selection-total, and cut crossings, and whose row covariance supplies scale-relative traction.  Without those statements, neither the non-even Gaussian lower-quantile transfer nor the exact-zero-scale branch is available, so the all-array coverage theorem cannot honestly be marked proved.

prose_updates.tldr: The accepted sharp-identification theorem continues to give \(\Theta_I(p)=[L(p),U(p)]\).  The round-two oriented repair passes the accepted \(K=4\) singleton-cell parity test: an explicit one-sided ray envelope has \(W(g)=0\) and \(W(-g)>0\), and a legal survivor-to-never-selected donor transfer dominates the witness's exact finite endpoint increment.  This shows that the earlier contradiction was caused by the even statistic \(\max_\nu|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}z|\), not by orientation itself.  The all-array theorem nevertheless remains unproved because no global row-by-row proof of oriented legal-envelope domination, covariance traction, and relative lower-quantile transfer has been established at simultaneous capacity, selection-total, and cut faces.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent settles sharp identification for the finite ordered survivor-complier benefit interval.  Existing inference results either impose fixed-law differentiability, start from supplied asymptotically linear endpoint or standardized moment representations, or require geometric and positive-variance regularity that excludes changing support and a jointly collapsing endpoint scale.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary-instrument model permits exact capacity geometry and common multinomial Gaussian calibration, but legality makes the local derivative envelope intrinsically oriented at binding selection-total faces.  The explicit \(K=4\) calculation now distinguishes this one-sided issue from the separate simultaneous-face and relative-quantile problems.
project_justification.fill: This round supplies an explicit oriented parity and finite-curvature certificate on the previously fatal singleton-cell witness.  It does not claim uniform coverage: the remaining contribution would require a complete finite legal transfer matrix proving pointwise oriented domination and scale-relative covariance traction through every simultaneous face, followed by a non-even lower-quantile theorem.  No support, cut-gap, cell-mass, or variance floor, screening rule, or deterministic guard is introduced.

prose_updates.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith survivor-complier benefit result supplies the exact sharp endpoint formula and full-law sharpness; identification is imported rather than reproved.  Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) support conditional instrument randomization, treatment consistency, and no defiers, while Dong and Heiler (2026) support treatment-mediated selection and outcome consistency together with covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity.  The fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap bound and fixed \(m_*\) denominator floor are uniform-class strengthenings here.  Fang and Santos (2019) and Hong and Li (2018) explain derivative-resampling methods, but their generic results do not construct the required nearby legal observed laws.  Frandsen and Pond (2025), Imai and Okamoto (2026), and Andrews and Guggenberger (2009) begin from regular or standardized representations that do not resolve the present one-sided legal-face problem.  The old scale-free unsigned-Gaussian lemma does not establish anti-concentration or quantile transfer for the required non-even maximum.  The new certificate only verifies the oriented mechanism on one explicit legal face and is not a substitute for that global theorem.
prose_updates.interpretation: The proposed rectangle targets simultaneous coverage of the observed-law sharp endpoint pair \(\Phi(p_n)=(L(p_n),U(p_n))\); it does not redefine the causal probability \(\theta_B\).  The imported identification theorem continues to yield \(\Theta_I(p_n)=[L(p_n),U(p_n)]\).  Exact common-Gaussian calibration on separated regular faces and the existing width calculations remain distinct results.  On the accepted boundary witness, orientation correctly distinguishes a legally inward flat direction from the opposite endpoint-changing direction, but this local success does not establish honesty over arbitrary triangular arrays.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The symmetric probe failure is repaired on its original \(K=4\) witness by an explicit oriented ray and legal latent transfer.  The unresolved obstruction is now the simultaneous-face certificate.  At raw-capacity zeros, selection-total ties, and tied threshold cuts, a candidate signed face row can be canceled by other active numerator or denominator terms outside its originating directional cone; consequently its positive part is not automatically pointwise below \(E_{p,r}\).  Donor transfers also alter two capacity margins, so covariance traction cannot be inferred from an abstract spanning argument.  Until every such row is legalized and the non-even Gaussian lower quantile is transferred at relative scale, the uniform theorem and exact-zero-scale branch remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Sharp identification is imported from the accepted parent and is not a contribution of this note.  The separated regular-face calibration, root-\(n\) width calculations, and diagnostic arrays are not overturned.  This round proves only that the explicit singleton-cell counterexample is compatible with an oriented repair, including exact nearby-legal-base domination of its finite increment.  It does not prove the global oriented comparison or all-array uniform joint coverage.  No individual support, survivor-cell, cut-gap, or variance floor and no screening or deterministic guard has been added.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the desired headline theorem: one common-Gaussian rectangle would cover both sharp endpoints uniformly without individual support, gap, or variance lower bounds.
statement_notes.gap: The accepted \(K=4\) counterexample now has an explicit oriented repair, but the theorem still lacks a complete simultaneous-face legal transfer matrix, pointwise oriented envelope domination, covariance traction, and a scale-relative conditional lower-quantile proof for the resulting non-even maximum.
statement_notes.consumer: Applications may use the separately proved regular-face and width results, but they cannot yet report the proposed rectangle as uniformly honest over arbitrary changing-support and tied-face arrays.
